pages.text: Upgrade slots grow with tier, from 3 to 8. Shift+Right Click a module onto the machine, or drop it into a slot:$(li)$(item)Speed$(): faster printing$(li)$(item)Efficiency$(): less FU per print$(li)$(item)RF Efficiency$(): less power$(li)$(item)Buffer$(): bigger RF tank$(li)$(item)Redstone$(): signal while working$(br2)Max $(l)4$() of a type, and only $(l)1$() Redstone.
$(item)Efficiency Upgrade$(): trims the tier's print markup. $(l)4 of them = break-even$() (1:1) on a $(l)Tier 4+$() machine: the print costs exactly what the matter is worth, and never less.
$(item)RF Efficiency Upgrade$(): ×0.85 RF cost per module.
$(item)Redstone Module$(): the machine reports when it is busy. Max $(l)1$() per machine.

pages.title: Redstone Output
pages.text: With a $(item)Redstone Module$() the machine emits a $(l)full-strength$() signal from all six faces $(l)while working$(), and nothing otherwise.$(br2)A $(l)paused$() machine reads 0, whatever the reason. So an $(l)inverted$() signal on a lamp lights the moment a print stalls.

pages.title: Wiring It Up
pages.text: On a $(l)formed$() fabricator $(l)any casing$() carries the signal, not just the controller, so you can take it off any face of the pad. A casing belonging to no formed machine stays dark.$(br2)It $(l)will not restart itself$(): while emitting, a rising edge never queues a start, so feeding its output back in cannot loop.

pages.title: Module Or Comparator
pages.text: A comparator already reads job progress for free. The module earns its slot where the two disagree:$(li)$(l)Idle$(): both 0$(li)$(l)Printing$(): module 15, comparator 1-15$(li)$(l)Stalled$(): module $(l)0$(), comparator non-zero$(br2)Comparator for a progress bar, module to catch a stall.

pages.title: Expected Blinking
pages.text: Printing on $(l)Auto$() into a hopper that drains slower than the machine fills the output will make the module's signal $(l)blink$(). That is accurate, not a bug: the machine really is alternating between printing and $(l)paused, output full$(), and the signal reports it faithfully.$(br2)Give the output somewhere faster to drain and it goes solid.

pages.title: Stacking
pages.text: Speed, RF, and Buffer stack $(l)multiplicatively$(): two Speed Upgrades print at 0.8 × 0.8 = $(l)64%$() time. Efficiency is $(l)linear$(): each module shaves a quarter of the tier's print markup, so $(l)4$() reach exact break-even.$(br2)Only $(l)Tier 4+$() machines have 4 slots, so only they can hit 1:1, and a Tier 4 must spend all four on Efficiency.

pages.title: Caps
pages.text: Max $(l)4 of each type$() per machine. The $(item)Redstone Module$() is the exception at $(l)1 per machine$(): a second copy is refused even with slots free.$(br2)It is also the only module with $(l)no numeric effect$(). The other four scale a rate; this one is a status output, so it changes nothing about how the print runs.$(br2)Rates are in the config for pack makers.
